info.title: Crypto Idea API
info.description:
Complete HTTP surface of the Crypto Idea backend (Firebase Cloud Functions v1 + Firestore security rules).

Three kinds of endpoint are documented:

1. **Public REST** (`/api/*`) — the `api` HTTP function. No authentication. Serves cached CoinGecko market data to the landing DCA calculator and the app, plus the public app config and the landing email-capture form. In production these are also reachable at `https://<your-domain>/api/*` via a Firebase Hosting rewrite (`firebase.json`).

2. **Callable functions** — Firebase `onCall` functions. The Firebase SDK POSTs `{"data": <input>}` and receives `{"result": <output>}`; on error it returns a non-2xx status with `{"error": {"message", "status", "details"}}`. Every callable verifies the caller's Firebase ID token server-side and acts on `context.auth.uid` — never a uid taken from the request body (no IDOR by design). **Admin** callables additionally require the verified `{admin:true}` custom claim.

3. **PayPal webhook** (`/paypalWebhook`) — the only unauthenticated inbound write. Every event is cryptographically verified against PayPal's verify-webhook-signature API before it is trusted.

Security model summary: Firestore rules are the authorization boundary (owner-only data, closed-shape user doc, users cannot write their own `tier`/`subscription`/`premiumLimits`/`deleted`). Secrets (CoinGecko / PayPal / email / Anthropic keys) live only in the server-side locked `config/app` Firestore doc or environment variables; they are never returned to a client and never shipped in the browser bundle.

servers.description: Local Firebase emulator — Cloud Functions base. Plaintext HTTP is expected here: the emulator serves on localhost only (never exposed to the network), so no TLS is used. This is the ONLY http:// surface — production (below) and the PayPal webhook are always HTTPS. REST endpoints are under /api/*; callables and the webhook are at /<functionName>.
Production — Cloud Functions base (replace YOUR_PROJECT at go-live). REST is also served at https://<your-domain>/api/* via the Hosting rewrite.

tags.name: MarketData
tags.description: Public, cached CoinGecko market data (prices, search, coin list, history, trending).

tags.name: Config
tags.description: Public non-secret app configuration read by the client on load.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Signed-in user self-service account actions (GDPR/CCPA, sessions, counters).

tags.name: Admin
tags.description: Admin-only operations. Require the verified {admin:true} custom claim. Kept in the PRIVATE repo.

get.summary: Current price + market data for one or more coins
get.description: Served from the shared cached coin universe; long-tail coins are refreshed on demand and folded back so upstream cost stays flat regardless of user count. Public and CDN-cached (max-age 120s).

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated CoinGecko coin ids (e.g. `bitcoin,ethereum`). Capped at 500; blank ids are dropped.

200.description: Map of coin id → price entry (only requested ids that resolved are present).

get.summary: Search the coin universe by id / name / symbol
get.description: Client-side-friendly search over the cached ~3,000-coin universe (no per-search upstream call). Returns up to 25 matches sorted by market-cap rank. Public, CDN-cached (max-age 300s).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term (lower-cased, capped at 100 chars). Empty returns an empty list.

get.summary: Full coin list (metadata + last price) for the landing DCA calculator
get.description: The whole cached universe (id/symbol/name/icon/rank + last price + 24h change), fetched ONCE by the landing page and served from the CDN for a day, so thousands of visitors add ~0 function calls. Public.
CoinGecko /search/trending, cached in its own doc (30-min TTL) and on the CDN. Backs the Search tab empty state. Public; an empty array signals the client to use its built-in fallback list.

Non-secret app config the client reads on load: maintenance flag, signups on/off, plan prices/limits, analytics IDs, legal (Termly) IDs. NEVER includes API keys or any secret. Public, short CDN cache (max-age 60s).

get.summary: Daily price history for one coin
get.description: Daily price series fetched once per coin and reused for every date range and every user (cached 30 days). Public, CDN-cached (max-age 86400s).

200.description: Array of `[timestampMs, price]` pairs (empty if unavailable — the client degrades to its built-in estimate).

post.summary: Landing-page email capture (public write)
post.description: The only public unauthenticated write. Forwards the email to the admin-configured provider (ActiveCampaign / GetResponse) server-side; the provider key never reaches the client. Protected by a strict per-IP budget (5/min), a honeypot field, and (at go-live) App Check/reCAPTCHA.

200.description: Accepted (also returned for a tripped honeypot, which is silently dropped).

502.description: Upstream email provider rejected the request.

post.summary: Start a PayPal subscription checkout for the signed-in user
post.description: Callable. Creates a PayPal subscription for `context.auth.uid` and returns the approval URL. Guards against re-buying the current tier and against duplicate submissions (60s per-uid cooldown).

200.description: Approval URL to redirect the user to.

500.description: internal / failed-precondition (already on this plan, plan not configured).

post.summary: Cancel the signed-in user's subscription (access runs to period end)
post.description: Callable. Cancels the caller's own PayPal subscription; the tier is NOT dropped immediately — access continues until the paid period ends. A premium user may target `pro`.

post.summary: Un-cancel a pending downgrade ("Keep my plan")
post.description: Callable. Clears the caller's own cancellation marker so the paid tier continues.

post.summary: Clear a pending Premium→Pro re-checkout marker
post.description: Callable. Clears the caller's own `subscription` re-checkout marker so the prompt doesn't recur across devices.

post.summary: Soft-delete the signed-in user's own account (GDPR/CCPA)
post.description: Callable. Marks the caller's account as trashed (recoverable for 30 days) and cancels billing. An admin who is one of the last 2 admins is refused.

post.summary: Restore the signed-in user's own soft-deleted account
post.description: Callable. Restores the caller's account if still within the 30-day grace window.

post.summary: Revoke all of the signed-in user's sessions
post.description: Callable. Revokes the caller's own refresh tokens so every device must re-authenticate.

post.summary: Export all of the signed-in user's own data (GDPR/CCPA)
post.description: Callable. Returns the caller's profile and full portfolios/coins/transactions tree.

post.summary: Recompute the signed-in user's aggregate counters from real docs
post.description: Callable. Recomputes portfolioCount/coinCount/txCount for the caller's own tree, fixing drift that could fire a false limit.

post.summary: [EMULATOR ONLY] Set the caller's own tier for local testing
post.description: Callable. HARD-gated to the emulator (`FUNCTIONS_EMULATOR === 'true'`); refuses with permission-denied in production. Lets a developer exercise Pro/Premium caps locally where no PayPal webhook exists. Not a production endpoint.

post.summary: Aggregate usage & revenue stats (admin)
post.description: Callable, admin-only. Returns aggregate counts and revenue — no personal data or holdings.

post.summary: Full users list — operational data only (admin)
post.description: Callable, admin-only. Merges Auth + profile (tier, disabled, admin, portfolioCount, joined, deleted). Never returns holdings. Capped at 5000.

post.summary: Look up one user by email (admin)
post.description: Callable, admin-only. Operational data only (tier, status, usage) — not holdings.

404.description: not-found — no user with that email.

post.summary: Set a user's tier (admin)
Set a user's per-user custom limits (admin)
post.description: Callable, admin-only. Each value is clamped to the product hard ceiling (coins ≤ 1,000) so a custom limit can only raise WITHIN — never past — the ceiling. Empty object clears the override.

post.summary: Suspend / un-suspend a user (admin)
post.description: Callable, admin-only. Disables the Auth account and revokes tokens; freezes the paid clock. Cannot target the caller's own account.

500.description: failed-precondition — can't suspend your own account.

post.summary: Hard-delete a user + all their data (admin, GDPR erasure)
post.description: Callable, admin-only. Recursively deletes Firestore data and the Auth account. Refuses self-target and refuses to drop below the minimum admin count.

post.summary: Soft-delete a user to the 30-day trash (admin)
post.description: Callable, admin-only. Recoverable soft-delete; cancels billing. Refuses admin targets (demote first).

post.summary: Restore a soft-deleted user from trash (admin)
Revoke a target user's sessions (admin)
Grant / revoke the admin claim (admin)
post.description: Callable, admin-only. Sets `{admin:true|false}` on another user by email. Refuses to drop below the minimum admin count on revoke.

post.summary: Read the recent admin audit log (admin)
Read saved app config to pre-fill Settings (admin)
post.description: Callable, admin-only. Secrets are returned as boolean set-flags ONLY (e.g. `secretSet`, `apiKeySet`, `anthropicKeySet`) — the secret values never leave the server.

post.summary: Save app config / API keys (admin)
post.description: Callable, admin-only. Writes the locked `config/app` doc. A blank secret field keeps the saved value (`keep()` idiom); secrets are never echoed back. Clients can never read `config/app` (Firestore rules deny all access).

post.summary: Inbound PayPal subscription webhook (signature-verified)
post.description: PayPal posts subscription lifecycle events here. Every event is cryptographically verified against PayPal's verify-webhook-signature API BEFORE any DB write; unverified events are rejected. Idempotent (each event id processed once). Not called by clients.

FirebaseAuth.description: The signed-in user's Firebase ID token. The Firebase callable SDK sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>`; the function verifies it server-side and reads `context.auth.uid`. Admin operations additionally require the verified `{admin:true}` custom claim on that token.

CallableError.description: Firebase callable error envelope (returned with a non-2xx HTTP status).

status.description: Canonical status, e.g. UNAUTHENTICATED, PERMISSION_DENIED, INVALID_ARGUMENT, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, FAILED_PRECONDITION, NOT_FOUND, INTERNAL.

PricesResponse.description: Map of coin id → price entry.

hp.description: Honeypot field — must be empty. Any value is silently dropped.

downgradeTo.description: Only a premium user may target pro.

result.description: Secrets appear ONLY as boolean set-flags — never the values.

data.description: A blank secret field (keys.coingecko, keys.paypalSecret, keys.anthropicKey, email.apiKey) KEEPS the currently-saved value.

PayPalEvent.description: A PayPal webhook event. Only trusted after signature verification.
